title: CatPortrait: Taming Video Generative Models for Portrait Animation via In-context Conditioning
title_zh: CatPortrait：通过上下文条件约束驯服视频生成模型以实现肖像动画

paragraphs.en: Recent video generative models have shown strong capability in synthesizing high-quality and temporally coherent videos. Yet, adapting them for controllable portrait animation remains nontrivial, as existing methods typically rely on architectural changes or extra conditioning modules, increasing complexity and reducing compatibility with pretrained models. We present CatPortrait , a simple and effective framework that enables controllable portrait animation via 3D face guidance as in-context conditioning. CatPortrait preserves the original video generation backbone and injects structured 3D facial guidance into the input space through spatial concatenation, allowing pretrained image-to-video models to animate portraits without sacrificing their pretrained priors. CatPortrait supports both video-driven and audio-driven portrait animation within a unified framework. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CatPortrait achieves competitive or superior results across both settings.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的视频生成模型在合成高质量且时间连贯的视频方面展现出强大能力。 然而，将其应用于可控的人物动画仍然并非易事，因为现有方法通常需要依赖架构修改或额外的条件模块，从而增加复杂性并降低与预训练模型的兼容性。 我们提出了 CatPortrait，一个简单而有效的框架，它通过作为上下文条件的三维面部引导实现可控的人物动画。 CatPortrait 保留了原有的视频生成主干网络，并通过空间拼接将结构化的三维面部引导注入输入空间，使预训练的图像到视频模型能够在不牺牲其预训练先验知识的情况下对人物进行动画化。 CatPortrait 在一个统一框架内支持由视频驱动和音频驱动的人物动画。 大量实验表明，CatPortrait 在这两种设置中均取得了具有竞争力或更优的结果。

paragraphs.en: Portrait animation, also known as talking head generation, aims to synthesize realistic facial videos driven by audio or reference motion while preserving identity and visual fidelity. It enables applications such as digital avatars, virtual meetings, and content creation, yet remains challenging to achieve both high quality and controllability.
paragraphs.zh: 肖像动画，也称为“对话头像”生成，旨在通过音频或参考动作驱动，合成逼真的面部视频，同时保留身份特征和视觉保真度。 它支持数字虚拟形象、虚拟会议和内容创作等应用，但要同时实现高质量和可控性仍然充满挑战。

paragraphs.en: Recent video foundation models [ wan2025wan , kong2024hunyuanvideo , ni2026seeing , li2026learning , li2026reward , liang2026teleboost , li2025growing , liang2026integrating ] can generate high-resolution and temporally coherent videos thanks to large-scale pretraining. However, directly adapting them to portrait animation is non-trivial: unconditional generation lacks precise motion control, while existing controllable methods [ hallo , xportrait , aniportrait , hunyuanportrait ] often introduce adapters, cross-attention branches, or modality-specific networks, increasing complexity and partially reducing the generality of pretrained models.

paragraphs.en: We revisit portrait animation from the perspective of in-context conditioning (ICC) and propose CatPortrait , which controls pretrained image-to-video models by spatially concatenating texture-free 3D facial guidance in the input space. Leveraging the strong reconstruction capability of modern VAEs [ wan2025wan ] and the disentangled representation of 3DMMs [ 3dmm ] , CatPortrait enables controllable portrait animation without modifying the video backbone.

paragraphs.en: CatPortrait unifies video-driven and audio-driven animation in a single framework. For video-driven animation, identity coefficients are extracted from the reference portrait and motion coefficients from a driving video; for audio-driven animation, a lightweight audio-to-FLAME model predicts motion from speech. The coefficients are rendered into a guidance video and concatenated with the visual input to synthesize the final talking-head video, introducing no additional parameters to the video generator. paragraphs.en: In-Context Conditioning. Recently, in-context conditioning (ICC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for controllable video generation and editing [ ju2025fulldit , video_icl , ju2025editverse , cai2025videocanvas , catvton ] . Instead of introducing task-specific adapters or auxiliary control branches, ICC-based methods place reference content and control signals directly in context, allowing pretrained video diffusion transformers to model the target output jointly with the provided conditions. Early evidence shows that video diffusion transformers can exhibit in-context generation capability under simple spatial or temporal concatenation with minimal tuning. More recent works further unify diverse control signals as a single token sequence processed by full self-attention, enabling multi-task video generation and editing without specialized architectural modifications. This line has also been extended to broader multimodal settings and finer spatio-temporal control, such as arbitrary patch-based video completion [ spatialtemp-freq , neuroevolution , vlm ] .
paragraphs.zh: 上下文条件约束。 近期，上下文条件约束（ICC）已成为一种有前景的范式，可用于可控的视频生成与编辑 [ ju2025fulldit , video_icl , ju2025editverse , cai2025videocanvas , catvton ] 。 与引入任务特定的适配器或辅助控制分支不同，基于 ICC 的方法将参考内容和控制信号直接置于上下文中，使预训练的视频扩散变换器能够与所提供的条件共同建模目标输出。 早期证据表明，视频扩散变换器在简单的空间或时间拼接下，经过极小程度的微调即可展现出上下文生成能力。 更近期的研究进一步将多样化的控制信号统一为单个令牌序列，由完整的自注意力机制处理，从而无需专门的架构修改即可实现多任务视频生成与编辑。 这一方向也已被扩展到更广泛的跨模态场景以及更精细的时空控制，例如任意的基于分块的视频补全 [ spatialtemp-freq , neuroevolution , vlm ] 。

paragraphs.en: Our work is inspired by this emerging ICC perspective, but differs from prior token-level or patch-level formulations in a fundamental way. Rather than targeting generic video editing or arbitrary spatio-temporal completion, CatPortrait instantiates ICC for portrait animation using a structured 3D facial prior. Specifically, we render disentangled 3DMM-based facial motion into a guidance video and inject it through spatial concatenation in the input space. paragraphs.en: We build CatPortrait on top of a pretrained image-to-video model and adapt it for portrait animation without modifying its architecture. As illustrated in Fig. 1 , given a reference portrait and a driving signal, we first estimate FLAME coefficients, where the identity is determined by the reference portrait and the facial motion is driven by either a video or speech input. Specifically, these coefficients are parameterized as ( β , ψ , θ ) (\beta,\psi,\theta) , where β \beta controls identity, while ψ \psi and θ \theta encode expression and pose, respectively. We then render the estimated coefficients into a texture-free 3D face guidance clip that explicitly captures the target facial dynamics. The rendered guidance is spatially combined with the appearance context to form a composite clip, which is encoded by the pretrained video VAE into the latent space. During denoising, the guidance region is clamped as known context, and the model synthesizes the portrait region conditioned on the rendered 3D motion. Finally, the animated result is obtained by cropping the generated portrait half from the synthesized video.

paragraphs.en: This in-context conditioning design is effective for two reasons. paragraphs.en: In the more challenging cross-reenactment setting, CatPortrait achieves the best AED and Image Quality, and the second-best AKD. These results indicate that our method transfers facial motion faithfully across identities while maintaining strong visual quality. The gains on AED and AKD support the effectiveness of the proposed 3D guidance in decoupling motion from source appearance and recomposing it onto a target identity. Meanwhile, the best Image Quality score suggests that CatPortrait better preserves the generative fidelity of the pretrained video model under cross-identity control. CatPortrait does not achieve the best identity similarity, indicating that preserving fine-grained identity cues under large cross-identity motion transfer remains an important direction for improvement.

paragraphs.en: Audio-driven talking head generation. Hallo generally achieves reasonable lip motion, but may occasionally produce unnatural mouth shapes. paragraphs.en: Specifically, we study four aspects of the proposed framework. First, we investigate different spatial concatenation layouts, including left-right and top-bottom concatenation with different ordering of the RGB portrait input and the rendered structural guidance. Second, we replace the 3DMM-based guidance with 2D landmarks to examine whether the disentangled 3D facial representation is necessary. Third, we remove the identity replacement step at inference time, i.e., the rendered guidance is driven by the source identity instead of replacing the identity coefficients with those extracted from the reference portrait, in order to verify the role of identity-motion disentanglement in cross-identity reenactment. Fourth, we compare full-parameter fine-tuning and LoRA-based fine-tuning to analyze whether the proposed framework can be adapted in a parameter-efficient manner.

paragraphs.en: We present CatPortrait, a simple framework for controllable portrait animation that adapts a pretrained video foundation model without modifying its architecture. By representing facial dynamics with a disentangled 3D face model and injecting texture-free 3D guidance through spatial concatenation, CatPortrait enables controllable facial animation while preserving the pretrained generative prior. Experiments show that it achieves competitive performance in both audio-driven and video-driven settings. We hope this work highlights the potential of 3D guidance as an in-context control signal for pretrained video generators.
